instruction: Write TypeScript code defining an interface User { id: number; name: string; email: string } and a typed function describeUser(user: User): string.
Write TypeScript code with a string literal union type Direction = "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" and a move function that only accepts those values.
Write TypeScript code declaring a tuple type Point = [number, number] and a function midpoint(a: Point, b: Point): Point.
Write TypeScript code typing function values: declare a type Comparator<T> and a function sorted(arr: T[], cmp: Comparator<T>): T[].
Write TypeScript code with an interface that has optional and readonly properties, and show which mutations the compiler rejects.
Write TypeScript code using typeof narrowing on a value typed string | number to implement a format(value: string | number): string function.
Write TypeScript code with a discriminated union Shape = Circle | Square | Rectangle and an area(shape: Shape): number function using the kind field.
Write TypeScript code using keyof typeof to derive a union of an object literal's keys and a typed getter.
Write TypeScript code with an index signature: type Scores = { [student: string]: number } and a function average(scores: Scores): number.
Write TypeScript code showing the difference between a type alias and an interface for the same shape, and where the alias is required (union types).
Write TypeScript code using unknown safely: a function parseJson(input: unknown) that type-checks before use, instead of any.
Write TypeScript code where a function returns void and callers must not use the result, plus a callback typed to return void that intentionally ignores its argument.
Write TypeScript function overload signatures for a flexible join() that accepts either (parts: string[], sep?: string) or (a: string, b: string).
Write TypeScript code typing a DOM event handler: add a click handler for HTMLButtonElement and show event.currentTarget typing.
Write TypeScript code implementing a type predicate function isNonNullable<T>(value: T | null | undefined): value is T and using it to filter an array.
Write TypeScript code using a class that implements an interface, with the compiler enforcing all members.
Write TypeScript code using an explicit this parameter to keep methods bound in an interface.
Write TypeScript code casting via unknown instead of any for a double assertion scenario, e.g. treating a serialized enum value safely.
Write TypeScript code defining a Result<T, E> union type and a safeDivide function returning it, plus a caller handling both branches.
Write TypeScript code with const enum alternatives: use a plain object with as const and a derived union type instead of enum, explaining the trade-off in a comment.
